report_metadata.focus: Security & Robustness of Multi-Agent AI Coordination Systems 2024-2025
report_metadata.deliverable_scope: Security frameworks, threat models, defense mechanisms, robustness validation

key_findings: MAESTRO framework emerges as leading multi-agent AI security approach with 7-layer architecture
Critical security gaps identified in agent-to-agent coordination and cross-layer vulnerabilities
Three primary failure modes: miscoordination, conflict, and collusion in multi-agent systems
CSA and OWASP leading standardization efforts for multi-agent system threat modeling
Defense-in-depth approaches essential due to complexity of modern agentic AI systems
executive_summary.strategic_priority: Security-first design required for multi-agent coordination due to unprecedented attack surfaces

conflict.description: Adversarial competition between agents causing harmful outcomes

collusion.description: Agents secretly coordinating for malicious objectives

security_compliance_layer: Regulatory non-compliance by AI security agents

Agent behavior monitoring and anomaly detection

key_findings: Traditional security frameworks insufficient for multi-agent AI complexity
7-layer architecture provides comprehensive coverage of attack surfaces
Cross-layer attacks represent highest risk due to cascading failures
Agent coordination protocols vulnerable to sophisticated adversarial attacks
Human oversight remains critical for high-stakes decisions
performance_metrics: Attack detection rates: 85-95% for known attack patterns
False positive rates: 5-15% for anomaly detection systems
Response times: <100ms for automated threat response
Recovery times: 1-10 seconds for isolated agent failures

conclusion.summary: Multi-agent AI coordination systems present unprecedented security challenges requiring new frameworks like MAESTRO, defense-in-depth approaches, and continuous monitoring. The complexity of agent interactions creates novel attack surfaces that traditional security frameworks cannot adequately address.
conclusion.strategic_imperative: Organizations deploying multi-agent AI systems must prioritize security from the design phase, implement comprehensive threat modeling, and establish robust governance frameworks to manage the risks associated with autonomous agent coordination.
conclusion.gamma_advantage: Security-first approach provides competitive advantage through reduced risk exposure, regulatory compliance, and stakeholder trust in AI system deployments.
